listings.rawTitle: Molecule 01 Eau de Toilette Spray with Metal Case 30ml
listings.description: Created with only one single ingredient, Iso E Super, Its chemistry adapts to the wearer and is different for every person. It is less an aroma and more an effect that lends an indefinable radiance to the wearer.It is characterised by a modern cedarwood note with a velvety sensation. The wearer may notice a pleasant, subtle velvety-woody note which will vanish, then re-surface after some time. This is due to the way it bonds with receptors. It's slow releasing to make way for a fresh charge of the molecule on the receptors.Iso E Super is a molecule that sits close to the skin to create a divine aura around the wearer. It does not exist in nature, It was created in a laboratory in 1973 and is designed to be worn by both men and women.Occasionally the wearer can not smell Molecule 01 and this can be due to a few reasons. Firstly the only ingredient is the aroma-molecule Iso E Super. This belongs to a group of fragrance materials such as musk and while some people are highly sensitive to it, a small few find them hard to smell. Also, the fragrance is slowly released and vanishes only to re-appear again later. While the wearer may experience this loss of scent others can still smell the molecule on them. Or lastly, it could be possible that the wearer is experiencing Hyposmia (smell blindness) in most cases this is temporary and a small break from wearing the fragrance can fix the problem.

listings.rawTitle: Rosemary Hair Oil
listings.description: It’s a TikTok beauty staple for hair routines (for good reason). Our 100% natural hair oil is packed with rosemary essential oil to encourage hair growth, whilst also moisturising and nourishing hair to leave it soft, smooth and shiny. Regular application can prevent hair loss for both male and female hair and pattern baldness, whilst its anti-inflammatory properties improve blood circulation to hair follicles and reduce hair fallout. TL;DR: If you’re looking to boost hair growth and leave your hair silky soft, this is for you. Here’s how the ingredients work: Castor oil: Known to boost hair growth by up to 5x the usual rate, castor oil is the essential ingredient for growth (and length). Grapeseed oil: Adding nourishment to dry hair and scalps, grapeseed adds much-needed shine and softness to your hair. Rosemary oil: Needs no introduction – boosts growth, blood circulation to the scalp, and reduces fallout or hair shedding. You can use this oil daily or every time you wash your hair – we’d recommend sticking to 6+ months of use to see the true benefits of a natural rosemary hair oil. How to use. Pre-wash treatment: Use on dry, unwashed hair before a shower by applying the product root to tips using the nozzle, focusing on areas such as the ends if they’re particularly dry. Leave on for at least an hour prior to washing, and wash off thoroughly (you may find that a double cleanse with shampoo is best). Once your hair is dry, run your fingers through your silky soft, shiny locks. Leave-in treatment: Apply a small amount through damp or dry hair and massage into the scalp from root to tip. For men, this oil can also be used as a beard oil for a finishing boost of shine and hydration. Finishing touch: Run a tiny amount of the oil – it’s packed of goodness, after all – through hair as a finishing touch to smooth down any fly-aways or frizz.

Don't worry if the roots grow outside the pot. In their native area, they grow in the crooks of branches, and use these aerial roots to absorb water from the air. They do not mind being over crowded in their pots, so you only need to repot them when the growth starts to suffer. A reporter by profession, he spends his free time working as an amateur detective, using his journalistic talents to compile facts and track down leads. In The Mystery of the Yellow Room, he saved the life of Mathilde Stangerson, the daughter of a prominent professor, from the clutches of Ballmeyer, a violent criminal mastermind gifted in the art of disguise. Unbeknownst to her father, Mathilde had married Ballmeyer while living in America before realizing he had been living under a false identity. Now believed to be dead, Ballmeyer fades into history as Rouletabille, his assistant Sainclair, and Mathilde return to their lives. Shortly after leaving for her honeymoon with Robert Darzac, however, Mathilde contacts Rouletabille with terrifying newstheir common enemy seems to have returned.
